decisions.quote: Considering rs613872, the most significant SNP in Caucasians, was absent in the Chinese FECD cohort, 23 we hypothesize this variant is not causal. Instead, here we show transethnic replication of the association of the expanded CTG18.1 trinucleotide repeat polymorphism, which is in the same LD block as rs613872, with FECD in the ethnic Chinese population.
decisions.reason: Both coders agree the study is a replication: it newly genotypes the CTG18.1 trinucleotide repeat polymorphism in a cohort of 57 Chinese FECD cases and 121 Chinese controls to re-test the published association between the CTG18.1 expansion in TCF4 and FECD.

decisions.quote: The strong association of the expanded CTG18.1 allele in the TCF4 gene with FECD in Caucasians, 25,27 demonstration of its cosegregation with the trait in Caucasian pedigrees, 27 and now transethnic replication of the association with similar effect sizes across populations are all compelling evidence that the repeat expansion is a causal variant.
decisions.reason: Reference 25 (Wieben et al., 2012; DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0049083) is the discovery study that first reported the strong association of the CTG18.1 trinucleotide repeat expansion in TCF4 with FECD and its greater specificity relative to rs613872 (also cited in the introduction and genotyping methods). Both the association of CTG18.1 with FECD and its specificity over neighboring TCF4 SNPs are directly re-tested in the Chinese cohort, and Reference 25 is explicitly cited in Discussion alongside Reference 27 as the Caucasian association replicated transethnically here.

decisions.quote: The strong association of the expanded CTG18.1 allele in the TCF4 gene with FECD in Caucasians, 25,27 demonstration of its cosegregation with the trait in Caucasian pedigrees, 27 and now transethnic replication of the association with similar effect sizes across populations are all compelling evidence that the repeat expansion is a causal variant.
decisions.reason: Although the shipped quote came from the abstract (which is absent from the parsed body text), the full text explicitly confirms a successful transethnic replication: the expanded CTG18.1 allele is strongly associated with FECD in the Chinese cohort (P = 4.7 x 10^-14, OR = 66.5, 95% CI: 12.6-350.1), and conditioning on CTG18.1 eliminates the association of all other TCF4 SNPs.

decisions.quote: In 2012, a strong association between a CTG trinucleotide repeat locus (CTG18.1) in intron 3 of the TCF4 and FECD was reported, which displayed greater specificity than rs613872. 25 The locus CTG18.1 was initially discovered by the repeat expansion detection assay and was found to be expanded in 3% of subjects in Caucasian pedigrees without known associated phenotype. 26 Expanded alleles with greater than 37 CTG repeats at this locus were found to be unstable. 26 Our group replicated the association with 120 FECD cases and 100 controls, finding that one copy of the expanded CTG18.1 allele increased risk of disease by 32.3-fold (95% confidence interval [CI], 13.4-77.6). 27
decisions.reason: Reference 27 (Mootha et al., 2014) is the authors' own prior replication of Wieben et al.'s (2012, ref 25) Caucasian CTG18.1-FECD association (plus familial segregation in Caucasian kindreds, which is not tested here). While the authors reuse their >=40-repeat cutoff and compare the Chinese odds ratio against Reference 27's Caucasian odds ratio, Reference 27 represents the same underlying CTG18.1-FECD association finding already captured by shipped row 71 (Wieben et al., 2012) rather than an independent omitted target.
